answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require proof of unique compute: each identity must regularly complete a fresh computational pulse, a short publicly verifiable workload bound to one hardware key, like a copper seal that cannot be copied. Identities grow like yarrow cuttings: each must show a distinct ongoing work trail, and duplicates sharing the same compute fingerprint are pruned. Forging a thousand fake agents then means paying for a thousand real machines and power bills, so attack cost scales linearly while honest participation stays cheap.
